title: Why Anthropic invited Hindu monk Swami Sarvapriyananda for Claude training meet
key_facts: Anthropic flew Swami Sarvapriyananda, head of the Vedanta Society of New York, to its San Francisco office earlier this year to discuss AI ethics, according to the monk's own account of the visit, which circulated this week.

He says the sessions brought together theologians, counsellors and mental health professionals, that participants saw unreleased material and signed non-disclosure agreements, and that he spent hours with one of the company's founders.
The Economic Times says these details come from his account and have not been independently confirmed by Anthropic.

Anthropic is reported to hold 'wisdom tradition circles' with Catholic, evangelical, Jewish, Sikh and African-philosophy thinkers, and to have met Cardinal Blase Cupich and Mormon apostle Gerrit W Gong, also unconfirmed secondhand reports.

Context given: Claude is guided by a 'constitution' of principles; co-founder Christopher Olah has spoken of 'moral formation'; the company has reportedly studied internal patterns resembling emotions but has not claimed Claude is conscious.
